notice.zdr: The model provider doesn't retain your prompts or use them for training (Zero Data Retention).
notice.local: The model runs on your device. Your data never leaves your machine.
notice.api30d: Does not train on your data, but retains it for up to 30 days for abuse prevention. Zero Data Retention is only available with an enterprise agreement.
notice.groq: Doesn't train on your data, but retains logs for abuse prevention for up to 30 days. Enable Zero Data Retention in your Groq account's Data Controls to prevent it.
notice.openrouter: OpenRouter forwards your request to another provider, so retention depends on the upstream provider. It doesn't store your prompts unless you opt in, and you can filter to Zero Data Retention providers in its settings.
notice.together: Together AI retains your data by default. Enable Zero Data Retention in your Together account to prevent it.
notice.zhipu: Z.ai (Singapore) states it does not store API content or train on it, but it operates outside the EU. Not recommended for personal data without contractual safeguards.
notice.zhipuChina: Configured against the China endpoint (open.bigmodel.cn): your data is stored in China under Chinese law and used to train models. Not recommended for sensitive data.
notice.google: The paid Gemini tier does not use your data. But the free tier (Google AI Studio) does use it to improve the product, with possible human review. Link billing to your project for data protection.
notice.anthropicConsumer: Claude Pro/Max trains on your conversations by default and retains them for up to 5 years. Turn off "Help improve Claude" in your account's privacy settings to prevent it.
notice.openaiConsumer: ChatGPT Plus/Pro trains on your conversations by default. Turn off "Improve the model for everyone" in your account's Data Controls to prevent it.
notice.minimax: MiniMax's data policy is opaque: it doesn't specify whether it trains on your data or where it stores it, and its parent company is in China. Not recommended for sensitive data.
notice.unknown: We haven't classified this provider's data policy. Treat it as if it retains your data.

buckets.title: Time buckets
buckets.body: Each KPI is computed across the selected period sliced into hourly buckets. A single turn that spans midnight contributes proportionally to both buckets.

tokens.title: Tokens counted
tokens.body: Aggregate of input + output tokens across every turn in the period. Cached tokens are NOT double-counted — they appear separately in the Cache & savings section.

agentActive.title: Agent-active vs user-active
agentActive.body: Agent-active sums duration per agent (so parallel agents add up). User-active coalesces overlapping intervals per user (so concurrent agents do not double count). Toggle the time metric in the filters.

costInfo.title: How Cost is computed
costInfo.body1: Cost is estimated locally from token counts (real, reported by the provider) multiplied by the pricing tables embedded in ai-tokenizer. It is NOT the amount the provider actually bills you.
costInfo.body2: Accuracy by provider: Anthropic / OpenAI / Google — close to the billed amount (within pricing-table drift). Auto-cache providers (OpenAI gpt-4o+, Codex OAuth, Cloudflare, Fireworks, OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible) — over-estimated, because their cache discount isn't visible to the adapter. Models without an entry in the table — counted as $0 (false negative; pricing unavailable).
costInfo.body3: The hero metric of this dashboard is Agent-hours because that is the unit Teros bills in (h/user/month, per the quota model). Cost stays as a secondary indicator.

quotaBurn.title: Quota burn
quotaBurn.subtitle: Agent-hours invested per user vs allocation
quotaBurn.emptyState: No agent activity in this billing period yet. Quota defaults to {{quota}} h/user/month until per-user billing schema lands.
quotaBurn.selectUserHint: Select a user above to see their burndown with consumption trajectory, projection and exhaustion forecast.
quotaBurn.overBudget_one: ⚠ {{count}} user on pace to exceed quota ({{names}}).
quotaBurn.overBudget_other: ⚠ {{count}} users on pace to exceed quota ({{names}}).
quotaBurn.infoParagraph1: Quota is hard-coded to {{quota}}h/user/month during the preview phase.
quotaBurn.infoParagraph2: Per-user override will live in `users.billing.agentHoursQuota` or Stripe metadata once the billing schema lands. Current display lets admins forecast trends without waiting for billing.

cacheSavings.title: Cache & savings
cacheSavings.subtitle: Prompt caching effectiveness across providers
cacheSavings.activeProvidersOnly: Among providers with Teros-active caching only: {{ratio}}% hit ratio ({{cached}} of {{total}} tokens).

autoCacheInfo.title: Why some providers show 0% but still have cost
autoCacheInfo.body: Providers marked `auto` cache internally but don't expose cached tokens via `LLMResponse.usage`. Their Cost already reflects the discount applied by the provider, but the ratio isn't visible in local metrics.

mechanismInfo.title: How caching works in Teros
mechanismInfo.intro: Each provider has its own upstream caching mechanism. Teros applies cache hints differently depending on the adapter.
mechanismInfo.activeBody: Teros sends explicit `cache_control` (mod-N=20 over system + tools + previous messages). Cached tokens visible. Applies to: Anthropic, Anthropic OAuth, MiniMax.
mechanismInfo.autoBody: The provider caches on its own (without Teros asking); the discount is applied to the billed cost but cached tokens are NOT extracted by the current adapter. Applies to: OpenAI (gpt-4o+), Codex OAuth (gpt-5), Cloudflare Workers AI (incl. Kimi K2.5/K2.6 with prefix caching), Fireworks AI (Kimi K2.6 and others), OpenRouter passthrough, OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
mechanismInfo.offBody: No active caching. The full input is paid every turn. Applies to: Gemini (Context Caching API exists but Teros doesn't integrate it — gap), Ollama local, Ollama Cloud, Zhipu, Zhipu Coding, Groq, Teros internal.
mechanismInfo.kimiBody: Kimi K2.5 / K2.6 are Moonshot AI models accessible in Teros via Fireworks or Cloudflare. Both providers cache Kimi upstream with real discount, but Teros uses OpenAICompatibleLLMAdapter which doesn't yet extract `cached_tokens` from the response. Effective status: auto.
mechanismInfo.otherOptimizationsBody: Active across all providers: compaction (CompactionService trims history), prune (PRUNE removes old tool outputs), latest message window (20 msgs default), token budget enforcement (rejects inputs >90% of context window), reasoning tokens captured separately (o-series models).
mechanismInfo.costAccuracyBody: The Total cost (period) above is real — `estimateCostUsd` uses ai-tokenizer pricing tables (97%+ accuracy) with the right cache_read / cache_write ratios per model. We don't show a single '% saved' because it varies per provider (Anthropic ~90%, OpenAI auto ~50%, Gemini context cache ~25%, others 0%).

totalCostInfo.title: Total cost (period)
totalCostInfo.body: Real cost already discounted by every provider's cache pricing. We don't show a 'savings %' because the ratio varies per provider — Anthropic ~90%, OpenAI auto ~50%, Gemini ~25%, others 0%. The number below reflects what your account will actually be billed.

cacheWritesInfo.title: Cache writes (one-time premium)
cacheWritesInfo.body: Cache write tokens cost more than regular input tokens (typically 1.25× for Anthropic). They are the up-front investment that lets later turns hit the cache at a heavy discount. This metric shows the premium paid; the cache_read savings are reflected in the Total cost above.

tokenBreakdown.title: Token breakdown
tokenBreakdown.perSessionHint: Click any row in Recent sessions to expand its individual breakdown.

methodologyInfo.title: Token breakdown methodology
methodologyInfo.body: Heuristic per-category via `ai-tokenizer` (encoding by provider, 97%+ accuracy) scaled to the real `usage.inputTokens` reported by the provider (correction factor) — exact sum to the real input tokens; proportions approximate.
methodologyInfo.footer: Click a row in Recent sessions to see the individual breakdown.

tokenBreakdown.legacyNoTokenBreakdown: This session was recorded before per-session token breakdown was enabled.
